# The Single-Tax Model and the Second-Order Condition {#sec-app-soc-model}

This appendix presents the single-tax model that @sec-model nests, and derives the second-order condition (SOC) for the firm's problem, which translates into the curvature restriction on the detection function $q(e)$ used throughout the paper.

## The single-tax model {#sec-app-single-tax}

The single-tax model keeps every assumption of @sec-model except one: a single rate $\tau$ applies to both sales and purchases. The firm solves
$$
\begin{aligned}
  \max_{K,L,M,e}\;\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}] = \;&(1-\tau)\big(P_tK_{it}^{\alpha_K}L_{it}^{\alpha_L}M_{it}^{\beta}\exp(\omega_{it})-\rho_tM_{it}\big)-r_tK_{it}-w_tL_{it}\\
  &+\big[1-q(e_{it})\big]\tau\rho_te_{it}-q(e_{it})\phi\tau\rho_te_{it}-\kappa_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-app-st-profit}
which is @eq-profit with $\tau_S=\tau_P=\tau$. The tax rate drops out of the materials FOC,
$$
\beta K_{it}^{\alpha_K}L_{it}^{\alpha_L}M_{it}^{\beta-1}\exp(\omega_{it})=\rho_t/P_t,
$$ {#eq-app-st-foc-m}
so the gross log share, $\ln(\rho_tM_{it}/P_tY_{it})=\ln\beta-\varepsilon_{it}$, takes the place of the net share in @eq-share-net. The evasion FOC is @eq-foc-e with $\tau$ in place of $\tau_P$,
$$
\tau\rho_t\big[1-(1+\phi)\big(q(e_{it})+q'(e_{it})e_{it}\big)\big]=\frac{\partial \kappa_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}},
$$ {#eq-app-st-foc-e}
and firms for which $\tau\rho_t\le\partial \kappa_{it}(0,\omega_{it})/\partial e_{it}$ do not overreport.

## The second-order condition {#sec-app-soc}

### Setup

Recall the firm's problem in the two-tax model, @eq-profit. The firm chooses capital, labour, materials, and overreporting, but the analysis uses only two FOCs, for materials (@eq-foc-m) and for overreporting (@eq-foc-e). Capital and labour are predetermined or dynamic, and the model does not solve for them. A candidate solution is a strict local maximum if the Hessian of expected profit is negative definite at that point.

### The evasion margin is separable

Overreporting is separable from the input choices. The probability of detection, the cost of evasion, and the credit on overreported materials do not depend on capital, labour, or materials, so every cross-partial between $e_{it}$ and the inputs $X_{it}=(K_{it},L_{it},M_{it})$ is zero. The Hessian of expected profit is therefore block-diagonal,
$$
\nabla^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]=
\begin{bmatrix}
\dfrac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial e_{it}^2} & \mathbf{0}'\\[4pt]
\mathbf{0} & \nabla^2_{X}\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]
\end{bmatrix},
$$ {#eq-app-soc-hessian}
where $\nabla^2_{X}\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]$ is the $3\times3$ Hessian with respect to the inputs and $\mathbf{0}$ is a $3\times1$ vector of zeros. Whatever the input choices require of that block, the evasion margin adds a single condition,
$$
\frac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial e_{it}^2}<0,
$$
and places no restriction on the inputs, which place none on it. For materials, the only input whose FOC the analysis uses, the second-order condition holds because the output elasticity of materials is below one, $0<\beta<1$:
$$
\frac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial M_{it}^2}=(1-\tau_S)P_t\,\beta(\beta-1)K_{it}^{\alpha_K}L_{it}^{\alpha_L}M_{it}^{\beta-2}\exp(\omega_{it})<0.
$$

The rest of this appendix analyzes the SOC for $e_{it}$ on its own.

### The scalar condition

Differentiating the evasion FOC (@eq-foc-e) once more with respect to $e_{it}$,
$$
\frac{\partial^2\mathbb{E}[\pi_{it}]}{\partial e_{it}^2}=-\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)\Big(2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\Big)-\frac{\partial^2\kappa_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}^2}<0.
$$ {#eq-app-soc-full}

Rearranging, the SOC holds whenever
$$
\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)\Big(2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\Big)+\frac{\partial^2\kappa_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}^2}>0,
$$
a sum of two terms. It is therefore *sufficient* — not necessary — that either term alone be strictly positive:
$$
\frac{\partial^2\kappa_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})}{\partial e_{it}^2}\ge0
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)\Big(2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\Big)\ge0.
$$ {#eq-app-soc-split}

**Under this paper's headline cost function**, $\kappa_{it}(e_{it},\omega_{it})=e_{it}\exp\{\delta_0-\delta_1\omega_{it}+\delta_2\omega_{it}^2+\psi_{it}\}$ — linear in $e_{it}$ — the first term is identically zero, $\partial^2\kappa_{it}/\partial e_{it}^2=0$. The cost function therefore contributes nothing toward satisfying the SOC on its own; the entire burden falls on the second condition, the curvature of the detection function.

### The curvature restriction

Since $\tau_P\rho_t(1+\phi)>0$, the second condition in @eq-app-soc-split reduces to $2q'(e_{it})+e_{it}q''(e_{it})\ge0$. Economic theory imposes $q'(e_{it})>0$ (detection is increasing in overreporting) and $e_{it}>0$ for an interior evader, so dividing through by $q'(e_{it})e_{it}>0$ gives
$$
-\frac{q''(e_{it})}{q'(e_{it})}\,e_{it}<2.
$$ {#eq-app-soc-final}

This is a restriction on the **curvature of $q$ alone** — a firm's evasion cost never enters, given the linear-in-$e$ specification above. It says $q'$ may decline as $e_{it}$ rises (a concave detection function), but not too fast relative to its own level: the semi-elasticity of the marginal detection probability with respect to $e_{it}$ must exceed $-2$.

### Application to the candidate detection functions

@tbl-app-soc-forms applies @eq-app-soc-final to the headline detection function of @sec-counterfactual and to three alternative forms.

| | $q(e)$ | $q''(e)$ | $-q''e/q'$ | SOC holds when |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Scaled power (headline) | $(\lambda_{0,jt}e)^{\lambda_1}$, $0<\lambda_1<1$ | $\lambda_1(\lambda_1-1)\lambda_{0,jt}^2(\lambda_{0,jt}e)^{\lambda_1-2}$ | $1-\lambda_1$ | always ($0<1-\lambda_1<1$) |
| Linear | $\min\{\lambda e,1\}$ | $0$ | $0$ | always |
| Concave | $1-e^{-\lambda e}$ | $-\lambda^2e^{-\lambda e}$ | $\lambda e$ | $\lambda e<2$ |
| Convex | $\min\{(\lambda e)^k,1\}$, $k>1$ | $k(k-1)\lambda^2(\lambda e)^{k-2}$ | $1-k$ | always ($k>1\Rightarrow1-k<0<2$) |

: Second-order condition by functional form of $q(\cdot)$ {#tbl-app-soc-forms}

**Scaled power detection, $q(e)=(\lambda_{0,jt}e)^{\lambda_1}$, $0<\lambda_1<1$, $\lambda_{0,jt}=1/(\bar\lambda\bar M_{j,t-1})$** (headline specification, @sec-counterfactual): with $x=\lambda_{0,jt}e$, $q'(e)=\lambda_1\lambda_{0,jt}x^{\lambda_1-1}$ and $q''(e)=\lambda_1(\lambda_1-1)\lambda_{0,jt}^2x^{\lambda_1-2}$, so $-q''e/q'=1-\lambda_1\in(0,1)$. The SOC holds at every interior point, for any $0<\lambda_1<1$ and any scale; the binding constraint is the FOC's own ceiling $x<(1+\lambda_1)^{-1/\lambda_1}$.

**Linear detection, $q(e)=\min\{\lambda e,1\}$**: $q''(e)=0$ on the interior, so $-q''e/q'=0<2$ unconditionally — the SOC holds at every interior point, with no restriction on $\lambda e$ beyond the FOC's own ceiling ($\lambda e<1/2$ with $\phi=0$, from @eq-foc-e).

**Concave detection, $q(e)=1-e^{-\lambda e}$**: $q'(e)=\lambda e^{-\lambda e}$ and $q''(e)=-\lambda^2e^{-\lambda e}$, so $-q''e/q'=\lambda e$. The SOC requires $\lambda e<2$ — a genuine restriction, distinct from (and, for this functional form, looser than) the FOC's own ceiling $\lambda e<1$ implied by @eq-foc-e with $\phi=0$. Since $\lambda e<1\implies\lambda e<2$, the FOC ceiling is the binding constraint in practice; the SOC is automatically satisfied wherever the FOC has an interior solution at all.

**Convex detection, $q(e)=\min\{(\lambda e)^k,1\}$, $k>1$**: $q'(e)=k\lambda(\lambda e)^{k-1}$ and $q''(e)=k(k-1)\lambda^2(\lambda e)^{k-2}$, so $-q''e/q'=1-k$. Since $k>1$, this is always negative, hence always less than $2$ — convex detection satisfies the SOC unconditionally, for any $k>1$.

**Summary.** All four detection functions satisfy the second-order condition on the relevant part of their domain — scaled power, linear and convex unconditionally, concave provided $\lambda e<2$, which is already implied by that function's own FOC-ceiling. The choice among them is therefore not disciplined by the SOC; it is a modelling choice about the detection technology, addressed on economic grounds in @sec-counterfactual.

The derivation carries over to the single-tax model (@sec-app-single-tax) with $\tau$ in place of $\tau_P$: the rate scales the curvature term but does not change its sign, so @eq-app-soc-final is the same condition in both models.
